userStories.title: Reach the general agent with inherited model and advertise agent tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make bare-task and explicit general dispatch usable on the caller's model, with consistent card annotations and declared tools in the agent index.

**Motivation** — #2928: `nax-agents__run` with no `agent` and no `model` fails with `[chat] run requires agent, or model to run the built-in general agent`, and `agent: "general"` fails with `unknown agent general`.

**Approach** — `nax-agents__run` with no `agent` and no `model` runs the built-in general agent on the chat's current model. `agent: "general"` is the built-in general agent unless the catalog has an agent of that name. `modelFor("general")` follows the same rule. The tool description and the agents index say so, and each index entry for an agent that declares `tools` lists them. Doc comments that say the general agent needs a model (`subagent-runs.ts` `modelFor`, `agent-call-model.ts`, `builtin-agent.ts`, the `RunTarget` comment) and `GENERAL_AGENT_DESCRIPTION` are updated to say it runs on the caller's model unless one is passed.

`targetOf` returns the general target when `agent` is absent (with or without `model`); `NO_TARGET` is deleted. The provider's `run` resolves `agent: "general"`: `catalog.findAgent("general")` first, and the built-in general agent when that finds nothing.

`SubagentRuns.modelFor(agentName, override)`: an absent `agentName` is the general agent; `"general"` with no catalog agent of that name is also the general agent. Preserve resolveSubagentModel's existing inheritance, alias/tier handling and refused overrides.

`agentRunCall`: with no `agent` and no `model` key it returns `{ agent: undefined, override: undefined }`, so the card shows the general agent's inherited model. A present but non-string `model` (or `agent`) still returns undefined: a malformed call is not annotated.

`buildAgentsInstructions` third line: `When no agent fits, omit agent (or pass agent general): the task runs on the built-in general agent with your tools, on your model unless you pass model.` An entry with `tools` renders `- <name>: <description> (tools: <tools joined by ", ">)`, the agent file's `tools` as written; an entry with `tools: []` renders `(tools: none)`. Preserve description sanitization and existing index truncation.

`RUN_DESCRIPTION` target last sentence: `To run a task with no catalog agent, omit agent (or pass agent general): the task runs on the built-in general agent with your tools, on your model unless you pass model.` All preceding sentences stay unchanged.

**Scope** — In: agents-provider.ts, subagent-runs.ts model preview, agent-call-model.ts annotation, builtin-agent.ts wording, agents-builder.ts index and existing conflicting tests. Out: nested tools instruction section (US-003), workflow config (US-005), launch defaults (US-006). Running the general agent when the catalog has no agents (the agents provider advertises no tool then).

**Interface** —
```typescript
// RunTarget retains its failure and named-agent arms.
type RunTarget =
  | { readonly kind: "failure"; readonly result: ToolResult }
  | { readonly kind: "general"; readonly task: string; readonly model?: string }
  | { readonly kind: "agent"; readonly name: string; readonly task: string; readonly model?: string };

export function buildAgentsInstructions(entries: readonly { qualifiedName: string; description: string; tools?: readonly string[] }[]): string;
```

Existing resolveSubagentModel({ requested, parentModel, aliases, tiers }): `requested === undefined` resolves `{ model: parentModel, source: "inherit" }`. Keep using it rather than inventing a model default. Update the old RUN_DESCRIPTION assertion and replace AC-6/AC-7 in agents-provider.test.ts with one injected general run and no model; delete NEEDS_AGENT_OR_MODEL. Replace AC-17/AC-18 in agent-call-model.test.ts with inherited-model and label annotation through modelFor(undefined, undefined). Update only the old third-line expectation in agents-builder.test.ts; the other line assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: Report NaxError turn-end reasons in abandoned tool results
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Include an available structured turn-end reason in both abandoned-tool result paths without changing cancellation behavior.

**Motivation** — #2930: a long `code-reviewer` subagent run ended with `Tool "nax-agents__run" was abandoned: the turn ended.` and nothing says why the turn ended (user stop, turn deadline, session close).

**Approach** — `abandonedToolMessage(name, signal)`:

- `signal.reason` is a `NaxError`: `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended (<code>: <message>).`
- otherwise (a bare `abort()`, a non-`NaxError` reason): `Tool "<name>" was abandoned: the turn ended.` (today's text).

`invoke` and `runCodingTool` build their abandoned result from it, using the signal the call raced (`request.signal ?? deps.turnSignal()` / `ctx.signal`).

Which aborts carry a reason: the session turn controller (`agent-session-turn.ts`) aborts with a `NaxError` for a cancel (`AgentSession.cancel`, default reason `cancelled`; the chat's Esc goes through it), the session turn deadline, a stalled consumer and an iterator close; `AbortSignal.any` keeps the reason of the source that aborted first. The native adapter's own idle watchdog and whole-turn deadline (`native/session-adapter.ts`) abort with no reason and keep today's text; this is why #2930 is only partly addressed.

Use the existing shared NaxError class. The turn controller already uses `abortReason(code, message)`, a `NaxError` whose `code` is `AGENT_SESSION_CANCELLED` (message: the cancel reason, default `cancelled`; `iterator closed`; `session closed`), `AGENT_SESSION_TURN_TIMEOUT` (`turn deadline`) or `AGENT_SESSION_CONSUMER_STALLED` (`consumer stalled`). No controller reason changes are needed.

Both current abandoned outcomes are constructed before their races; evaluate the new message at abandonment time, not before abort, so in-flight reasons are observable. Preserve already-aborted handling, existing provider cancellation grace, late-settlement handling, answerFor wrapping and listener/timer cleanup. The InteractionHandler rejects with a NaxError on either error path; the surrounding tool batch turns that rejection into the tool's error result. Handler-level tests observe the rejection message, while the AgentSession integration observes the abandoned tool result as the turn ends, not an invented return value from onInteraction or turn_end.output. Existing tests abort with a bare `controller.abort()`, whose reason is not a `NaxError`, so they keep today's text.

**Scope** — In: session-interaction.ts module-exported helper, embedder invoke and coding tool outcomes, handler-level and real AgentSession cancellation regressions. Out: chat dispatch/tools text (US-002/US-003), workflow configuration (US-005). Keeping a long subagent run alive after its parent turn ends, or moving it to a background task (#2930 second half); this feature only records why the turn ended. The ACP twin of the abandoned message (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/tool-calls.ts`) keeps today's text. Attaching an abort reason to the native adapter's own idle watchdog and whole-turn deadline in `native/session-adapter.ts`.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts (module export, used by both abandoned paths)
export function abandonedToolMessage(name: string, signal: AbortSignal): string;
```

Keep this as a module export; no package-root public API expansion is requested. Use Node-compatible code and #src imports in nax-agent. Tests must show the regression failing against old code before implementation, use injected clocks for grace cases, and coordinate session.cancel() after a never-settling embedder tool has started.

userStories.title: Render workflow choices, fix-round budget and canonical feature paths
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry loaded chat.workflow choices and canonical feature-folder paths into the workflow instructions while preserving existing guidance.

**Motivation** — #2945: the workflow instructions name no paths, so specs land in `docs/specs/`, and review reports, fix-round reports and hand-off notes pile up as extra files.

**Approach** — `buildWorkflowInstructions({ workflow })` keeps every existing line and its order, edits lines 1 and 2 in place, and appends the new lines after the existing last line, in the order 3, 4, 5, 6. `N` is `workflow?.specFixRounds ?? DEFAULT_SPEC_FIX_ROUNDS`, written as an English word for 1-10 (`one` ... `ten`), capitalised at the start of a sentence. Here items 1 and 2 identify the loop and budget lines, not their zero-based positions in the source array; preserve the initial state-read line.

1. Loop line: `spec-review (usually two fix rounds)` becomes `spec-review (usually <N> fix rounds)`.
2. Budget line: `Two spec-review fix rounds are the default budget, not a limit: past two, ...` becomes `<N> spec-review fix rounds are the default budget, not a limit: past <N>, ...`; the rest of the line is unchanged.
3. New paths line, always present: `The spec for a feature is `<PROJECT_FEATURES_DIR>/<feature>/spec.md`, which is where the plan launch reads it. Spec-review findings and fixes stay in this chat and in the spec itself, so a spec round writes no report file; the PRD fidelity check (spec-review --prd) writes `<PROJECT_FEATURES_DIR>/<feature>/prd-fidelity-report.md`.`
4. New spec-agents line, only when `specWriter` or `specReviewer` is set (a choice with neither `agent` nor `model`, such as `{}`, counts as unset): `Spec-writing runs through nax-agents__run with <choice of specWriter>; spec-review runs with <choice of specReviewer> (chat.workflow).` A choice renders as `agent <agent>` and/or `model <model>` joined by ` and `; an unset choice renders `the agent you choose`; a choice with only `model` names `agent general`.
5. New profiles line, only when `plan.profiles` or `run.profiles` is non-empty: `chat.workflow sets the profiles for nax plan (<names>) and nax run (<names>); leave profiles empty on those launches and the card names them.` A step without profiles is omitted from the sentence. This line never names `nax bot review` or `nax bot fix`, so the one line that names all four billed commands stays unique.
6. New choices line, only when at least one of `plan.profiles`, `run.profiles`, `specWriter`, `specReviewer` is unset: `In this chat, where chat.workflow does not set them, the plan and run profiles and the spec writer and reviewer are the user's choice: nax-jobs__list returns the profile names; ask for the spec writer and reviewer when you propose spec-writing, and for the profiles in the same message that asks for plan approval.`

`cli/chat.ts` passes `workflow: config.chat?.workflow` to `createWorkflowProvider`.

All prompt text lives in `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/` (project rule). New instruction text states facts the agent can use; it adds no new prohibitions. Instruction text builds the feature folder from `PROJECT_FEATURES_DIR` (exported from `@/config`) rather than a literal, so the path has one source (`check-feature-dir-ssot` exempts `src/prompts/`, so this is a choice, not a gate).

`buildWorkflowInstructions` with no input, or no `workflow`, outputs today's text unchanged, followed by the paths line and the choices line (items 3 and 6). `createWorkflowProvider` takes `WorkflowProviderOptions` and uses `instructions: async () => buildWorkflowInstructions({ workflow: options.workflow })`.

**Scope** — In: workflow-builder.ts rendering, WorkflowProviderOptions/config forwarding, cli/chat.ts composition and existing text-preservation assertion rewrite. Out: agent dispatch and nested tools text (US-002/US-003), chat schema/types (US-005), launch/chain defaults and jobs instruction line 7 (US-006). Moving or renaming existing specs under `docs/specs/` or existing `prd-fidelity-review.md` files. Changing the spec-writing or spec-review skills themselves. `nax agents run` (`cli/agents-run-compose.ts`) creates its workflow provider without `chat.workflow`; it gets the default instructions only.

**Interface** —
```typescript
interface WorkflowProviderOptions extends FeatureStateOptions { readonly workflow?: ChatWorkflowConfig }
createWorkflowProvider(options: WorkflowProviderOptions): ToolProvider
buildWorkflowInstructions(input?: { readonly workflow?: ChatWorkflowConfig }): string
```

US-007 consumes `ChatWorkflowConfig` (US-005); its seam AC enters at the workflow provider's `instructions()`. The test "US-004 AC-11 retains the original lines, the fix-budget line (#2929), then the repo line" in workflow-builder.test.ts currently asserts exactly six lines. Rewrite it to the new invariant: the first six lines are unchanged and in order, followed by the paths line, then the choices line. The other tests in that file keep passing: with no input the existing lines keep their order; the paths and choices lines are appended after the last one, so the loop-order test still finds `spec-review`, `nax plan`, `nax run` and `nax bot fix` first in the loop line, and neither added line names all four billed commands or a cap word.

routing.reasoning: Deterministic prompt rendering and two existing composition seams; no permission, enforcement or session-lifecycle behavior changes.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "US-004 AC-11 retains the original lines, the fix-budget line (#2929), then the repo line" (`:219-232`) asserts `buildWorkflowInstructions()` is exactly the six current lines. Under US-007 the no-input output is those six lines followed by the paths line and the choices line, so the exact-text assertion fails against a correct implementation. US-007 owns rewriting it to the new invariant: the first six lines are unchanged and in order, followed by the paths line, then the choices line. The other tests in that file keep passing: with no input the existing lines keep their order; the paths and choices lines are appended after the last one, so the loop-order test still finds `spec-review`, `nax plan`, `nax run` and `nax bot fix` first in the loop line, and neither added line names all four billed commands or a cap word.

analysis:
This is an enhancement of the existing Bun/TypeScript chat orchestration, not a new workflow engine. It closes #2927, #2928, #2931 and #2945, and addresses only the reason-reporting half of #2930 under tracking issue #2946. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct source reads, Grep and Glob. References below describe the pre-change source; tests were inspected but not executed during PRD drafting.

Refine audit: all 92 numbered-list criteria in spec.md:382-495 are retained in their original stories and original order: US-001 AC1-AC9, US-002 AC1-AC15, US-003 AC1-AC8, US-004 AC1-AC7, US-005 AC1-AC12, US-006 AC1-AC23 and US-007 AC1-AC18. Regression qualifiers remain attached, including the invalid-name error staying unchanged, no-tools index entries, malformed-call passthrough without modelFor, unchanged permission/rules/memory/prompt order, no-workflow provenance/card behavior and the unique explicit-approval line. The six failure-table rows map respectively to US-001 AC5-AC6, US-001 AC9, US-002 AC5, US-005 AC6-AC11, US-006 AC16-AC17, and US-004 AC3-AC4; the config-validity row covers four invalid-value categories. Each story has a negative-path assertion: invalid feature name (US-001 AC9), malformed model (US-002 AC15), empty allowedTools and absent tools section (US-003 AC2/AC8), non-NaxError fallback (US-004 AC4), rejected config values (US-005 AC6-AC11), unknown configured profiles with no card (US-006 AC16-AC17/AC20), and omitted/empty choices producing no configured-agent line (US-007 AC10-AC11). All criteria are observable via return values, rejection messages, tool calls/events, rendered text or injected call arguments; no new feature behavior was invented. Refine corrections: restore both missing spec-recommended test context files for US-002/US-006; describe US-004 handler failures as NaxError rejections rather than returned ToolResults, matching session-interaction.ts:194 and :278; delimit the exact US-007 budget prefix to avoid requiring a spurious period after the comma; and classify US-002 as medium because it adjusts five existing modules without a new abstraction. Strict session/approval test strategies remain required. All eleven feature-level exclusions and all binding dependencies/workdirs are preserved; there are no story-local deferral blocks to hoist.

Architecture and constraints: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 defines injectable _deps for external calls; :90 describes prompt construction as belonging to src/prompts; :137 describes dependency boundaries. Keep all new instruction text in packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/, use existing barrels, and keep feature paths derived from PROJECT_FEATURES_DIR exported by packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:33. nax source is Bun-oriented; nax-agent shipped source must remain Node-compatible and use #src imports or explicit .ts relative extensions. US-004 is a module-local export, not a requested package-root API change, so do not unnecessarily expand the public API or change lockstep versions. The binding seven stories and their workdirs/dependencies are retained. US-001, US-002, US-004 and US-005 can start independently; US-003 follows US-002, while US-006/US-007 follow US-005. US-001/US-007 share workflow-provider.ts, US-002/US-003 share agents-builder.ts, and US-006/US-007 share workflow-builder.ts: retain each other's edits without introducing new dependency IDs.

US-001 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/workflow/workflow-provider.ts:23 already discovers sorted feature directories through _workflowProviderDeps and filters both validateFeatureName and featureDir. readState at :55 resolves a possibly nested target repo first, handles omitted feature as the existing list, and validates before any artifact read. The existence branch at :75 delegates existing directories or legacy .nax/specs/<feature>.md to readFeatureState. Only the absent-artifact branch at :78-81 changes; remove its 20-name failure formatting, not the protections or legacy behavior. packages/nax/src/chat/workflow/feature-state.ts:16 defines FeatureStateOptions; :22 defines FeatureState; :83 reads the full artifact state. Leave this reader and list shape unchanged; NotStartedFeature deliberately has fewer fields and stage not-started. New similar-features.ts is a pure case-sensitive Levenshtein helper over supplied names, threshold max(2, floor(query.length / 4)), distance then name ordering, capped at three. Suggestions must come from validated directories only. Existing workflow-provider tests at packages/nax/test/unit/chat/workflow/workflow-provider.test.ts:136, :204, :216 and :240 pin unknown-feature errors and must be replaced, not worked around; :144-198 preserve path-validation-first behavior and the stricter 64-character featureDir limit; :221 preserves legacy spec-only reading.

US-002 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/agents-provider.ts:9 holds the description, :15 the obsolete NO_TARGET, :48 RunTarget, :53 targetOf and :69 provider construction. The schema already requires task only; tools are still absent when the catalog has no agents (:91). Make absent agent dispatch general with optional override; explicit general must prefer catalog.findAgent before fallback. packages/nax/src/chat/builtin-agent.ts:13-30 defines the built-in origin nax-builtin, deliberately no model or tools, and currently has stale model-required wording. packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-runs.ts:115 already resolves override ?? agent.model against current().model, and :207 maps tools before calling runSubagent; :243 must mirror explicit-general fallback in modelFor. packages/nax/src/chat/agent-call-model.ts:26 currently suppresses a bare task call and can overlook a malformed model when agent is a string; validate present non-string keys before annotating. withAgentCallModel (:37) merges subagentModel and subagentModelSource metadata and must preserve other event fields. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/agents-builder.ts:17 renders the index with sanitized descriptions and a 150-entry cap; append raw declared tool names without translating them. Provider instructions already pass catalog.agents structurally, so ensure widening the builder input carries tools without changing resource discovery. Regression anchors: packages/nax/test/unit/chat/agents-provider.test.ts:251-290 freezes the old description and missing-target errors; packages/nax/test/unit/chat/agent-call-model.test.ts:85-105 freezes old no-annotation behavior and malformed model passthrough. Existing subagent-runs.test.ts, subagent-model.test.ts, builtin-agent-related tests and prompts/builders/agents-builder.test.ts cover model resolution and rendering. General-agent availability changes session dispatch but must not bypass inherited permissions, ACP selection or unknown-model refusal.

US-003 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-tools.ts:68 preserves undefined (inherit parent tools) versus [] (only always-on tools) and translates Skill to nax-skills__*. Read it but do not alter mapping. packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-runs.ts:207-217 already passes mapped allowedTools to runSubagent. packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts:38 exposes allowedTools and :102 passes it to the native backend, but :115 does not pass it to buildSubagentInstructions. Thread that value into the builder; do not re-map or change grants. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/agents-builder.ts:9 defines the instruction input, and :62 builds permission/rules/memory/agent-prompt sections. The new optional section goes immediately before the agent prompt, preserving undefined output byte-for-byte. Existing packages/nax/test/unit/chat/subagent-session.test.ts and test/unit/prompts/builders/agents-builder.test.ts are the principal builder and createAgentSession seams; host-subagents.test.ts and subagent-session-acp.test.ts remain regression coverage, not a request to change ACP tools.

US-004 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts:12 imports the shared NaxError identity. invoke (:162) and runCodingTool (:283) currently precompute abandoned outcomes before the signal aborts; merely replacing their literals at construction time would capture no reason for in-flight calls. Build messages lazily when the abort race or grace expires, and on the already-aborted path, using exactly the signal raced. runEmbedderTool (:178) selects request.signal ?? deps.turnSignal(); coding calls do the same. Preserve runSafely exception handling, answerFor error wrapping, current-call cleanup, cancellation grace normalization and timer/listener cleanup. raceCancelGrace (:226) deliberately allows a provider to settle inside its grace; the new reason must not replace that outcome. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:27 names the cancellation/deadline/stalled codes; :73 constructs NaxError reasons; :237-275 retains first-abort semantics for iterator close, deadline, stalled consumer and cancellation. These reasons already exist, so leave controller behavior and native idle/whole-turn timers unchanged. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/session-interaction-cancel-grace.test.ts:49-86 provides the fake-clock harness and :51 the old bare-abort message; bare abort assertions remain valid. Add direct helper cases and both handler paths, plus a createAgentSession integration regression with a never-settling embedder tool and session.cancel(). An integration test must coordinate on tool entry rather than wall-clock sleep. New regressions in nax-agent must be demonstrated failing on old code. Session/lifecycle work gets strict three-session-tdd.

US-005 findings: packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:90 defines the root Zod object and :462 uses BotConfigSchema.prefault({}); packages/nax/src/config/schemas-bot.ts:4 and runtime-types-bot.ts:13 illustrate split runtime/schema modules. Chat must differ from bot at the root: optional chat without default or prefault, optional workflow, and specFixRounds default only inside a present workflow. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types.ts:333 defines NaxConfig and :377 the bot field. Export the new runtime chat types from types.ts beside its bot exports (:43) and from index.ts beside its bot exports (:58); export DEFAULT_SPEC_FIX_ROUNDS from index.ts. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-argv.ts:34-35 supplies the exact profile/model regexes to mirror. Do not import launch modules into config to reuse patterns if that creates an upward dependency. Profile discovery is async at packages/nax/src/config/profile.ts:304; defer name existence checks until launch. packages/nax/src/config/merger.ts:53-60 already replaces arrays and recursively merges objects; loader.ts:155 overlays profile data, so no merger/loader algorithm change is required. Existing config schemas.test.ts and merge.test.ts cover defaults/layering; add focused schemas-chat tests for Zod issue paths and preserve DEFAULT_CONFIG key sets.

Keep this inspection seam; workflow-defaults.ts must own a separate _workflowDefaultsDeps leaf with the same listing body. jobs-launch.ts uses a type-only JobsProviderOptions import (:12), so importing a value from jobs-provider here would create a cycle with launchToolRun. Apply defaults after parsing and before prepareTarget; run unknownWorkflowProfile after preparation to preserve missing-spec/PRD error priority and before any approval. prepareRun (:167-196) already warns on an explicit profile chain differing from PRD routingProfile and already formats planned-profile fallback; config defaults must flow through this same comparison. launchReason (:253) centralizes existing card lines, which must stay byte-identical without config. prepareFinish (:202) remains publish-only; finish uses workflow.run and has no new independent key. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-tools.ts:51 resolves each step repo and plan spec; :62-85 builds argv through buildChainStepArgv. Apply defaults and profile existence validation there too, including PR-less bot steps, so persisted approval argv matches eventual individual launch argv and stepError retains the exact [chat] step N prefix. Do not require a PRD during proposal when an earlier plan step will create it. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:73 constructs the provider through _jobsHostDeps; pass options.config.chat?.workflow. Preserve mode-owned approval, busy/write guards and chain consent. Existing jobs-launch.test.ts:1-90 exposes injected approval/start seams; jobs-launch-chain.test.ts, chain-tools.test.ts, chain-tool-card.test.ts, chain-tools-repo.test.ts and jobs-host.test.ts cover integration surfaces. Add pure defaults tests plus actual plan and chain tool-run tests, not utility-only assertions.

US-007 findings: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts:7 currently returns six exact ordered lines; :59 builds separate jobs instructions. Preserve the first six default lines, edit only the two fix-round phrases when configured, append paths/spec-agents/profiles/choices in that order, and retain exactly one billed-command approval line. English number rendering is bounded by the config range 1-10. Use PROJECT_FEATURES_DIR from config rather than a literal, and DEFAULT_SPEC_FIX_ROUNDS from schema exports rather than a second default. Empty choices {} and empty profiles count as unset. packages/nax/src/chat/workflow/workflow-provider.ts:85/:102 constructs the provider and instructions closure; add WorkflowProviderOptions extending FeatureStateOptions and forward workflow into the builder without changing readState. The workflow/chat barrels currently export provider and FeatureStateOptions (packages/nax/src/chat/workflow/index.ts:2; packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:155); preserve old imports and expose the new options type as needed. packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts:270 constructs this provider behind deps.createWorkflowProvider and should pass the loaded session config. packages/nax/src/cli/agents-run-compose.ts:115 is another consumer and intentionally keeps default instructions. packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.test.ts:219-232 pins exactly six lines and needs the two appended default lines; other ordering/approval assertions must remain meaningful. cli/chat-resources.test.ts and workflow-provider.test.ts provide composition and instructions seams.

Compatibility and migration: no data migration, spec relocation or profile-format change. Existing config without chat must keep its parsed/default key set, existing workflow state lists and artifact reads remain intact, and launches without configured defaults keep today's argv/cards and PRD-profile fallback. The intentional API behavior changes are successful not-started state instead of an unknown-feature error and bare-task general dispatch instead of NO_TARGET; update their old assertions rather than retaining conflicting behavior. Configured profiles use the session's loaded workflow block but are validated against each resolved target repo; explicit launch overrides retain today's validation behavior. Avoid mutating readonly caller/config arrays, losing provenance during prepareTarget, validating unknown profiles before missing artifacts, or accidentally adding root defaults. No releases, changes to skills, background subagent execution, ACP abandoned-message changes or permissions changes are needed.
outOfScope: Keeping a long subagent run alive after its parent turn ends, or moving it to a background task (#2930 second half); this feature only records why the turn ended.
The ACP twin of the abandoned message (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/tool-calls.ts`) keeps today's text.
Loading a flow profile mid-session from a chat message ("use flow profile X"); a profile is selected with `nax chat --profile`.
Validating `chat.workflow` profile names at config load.
Running the general agent when the catalog has no agents (the agents provider advertises no tool then).
Moving or renaming existing specs under `docs/specs/` or existing `prd-fidelity-review.md` files.
Changing the spec-writing or spec-review skills themselves.
Classifying a subagent's question as a tooling blocker and rerouting it; the subagent is told its tools instead.
`finish` has no `chat.workflow` key of its own; it uses `run`.
`nax agents run` (`cli/agents-run-compose.ts`) creates its workflow provider without `chat.workflow`; it gets the default instructions only.
Attaching an abort reason to the native adapter's own idle watchdog and whole-turn deadline in `native/session-adapter.ts`.
